title: zenith-private-mesh-soleng-scratchpad
content:
Zenith (finance) — Private control-plane + on-prem inference nodes
Quick scratchpad for my implementation notes, actions, and config fragments. Use this as the canonical dev scratchpad until I move finalized content to Confluence.

Context / constraints:
- Regulated customer, must keep PII inside their VPC/on-prem cluster.
- Need HSM-backed key management (AWS CloudHSM or Vault HSM) for model keys and audit signing.
- Retention: 7 years audit logs (compliance asks).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 150 ms for short prompts (<128 tokens).
- Throughput target: 200 concurrent sessions baseline, burst to 500.
- Model: open variant 'rw-fast-1.1' quantized int8, fallback to cpu-quant when GPUs degraded.

Daily notes (iterative)
2026-03-10 09:30 — Kickoff with Zenith infra
- Confirmed they want private control plane in their AWS account (VPC peering for managed plane) + on-prem inference nodes in colo.
- Action: ask SecOps for approved HSM vendors (Priya).
- Blocker: customer network team requires IP allowlist for control plane; need final CIDR list from us.

2026-03-11 14:15 — Infra scoping call
- Decided on hybrid routing: primary -> private-hosted nodes in Zenith colo (k8s), fallback -> dedicated Redwood capacity in eu-west-1 (if colo capacity lost).
- Need the following: model pinning config, rollout canary rules, and automatic fallback policy.
- Action: Add canary policy: 5% traffic to new model for 24h, if error rate > 1% rollback. (Ticket: JIRA ZEN-92).

Implementation TODOs (short):
- [ ] Produce minimal redwood-config snippet for Zenith (see below).
- [ ] Obtain HSM vendor list + integration plan (Priya).
- [ ] Finalize IP CIDR range for control-plane egress (Liam -> SecOps).
- [ ] Write deployment playbook for on-prem node bootstrap (include KMS certs).
- [ ] Verify audit log forwarder to S3 Glacier-compatible bucket (7yr retention).
- [ ] Smoke test latency with 1K random short prompts (script: perf/smoke/zenith-short.sh).

Quick redwood config (example) — keep lightweight for handoff
# redwood-zenith.yaml (fragment)
# flat text: to be copied into customer's control plane onboarding script
redwood:
  customer: "zenith-finance"
  deployment:
    mode: "private"
    control_plane:
      location: "managed-in-customer-aws"
      allowed_cidrs: ["10.11.0.0/16", "52.21.0.0/20"] # placeholder - replace after SecOps list
    inference_nodes:
      - location: "zenith-colo-1"
        k8s_namespace: "redwood-zenith"
        node_pool: "g5-48gb"
        autoscale:
          min: 3
          target: 12
          max: 40
    model_policy:
      default_model: "rw-fast-1.1-int8"
      fallbacks: ["rw-fast-1.1-cpu-quant", "rw-compact-0.9"]
    rollout:
      canary_percent: 5
      canary_window_hours: 24
      error_threshold_pct: 1
  kms:
    provider: "vault-hsm"
    endpoint: "https://vault.zenith.internal"
    key_name: "redwood/zenith/master"
  audit:
    forwarder: "s3"
    bucket: "s3://zenith-redwood-audit"
    retention: "7y"

Notes on KMS/HSM integration
- We need to support both AWS CloudHSM and HashiCorp Vault w/ HSM-backed keys. Customer prefers Vault HSM.
- Integration checklist: 
  - TLS certs pinned to company CA.
  - Mutual TLS for redwood-agent <-> vault.
  - Key rotation policy: 90 days (customer requirement).
  - Audit events must include key-id, operation, actor, timestamp.

Kubernetes kube manifests / annotation snippet (for on-prem nodes)
# Use node selector + taint for redwood workloads
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: redwood-runtime-0
  namespace: redwood-zenith
  annotations:
    redwood.com/replica-type: "inference-gpu"
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    nodepool: "g5-48gb"
  tolerations:
    - key: "dedicated"
      operator: "Equal"
      value: "redwood"
      effect: "NoSchedule"

Service routing notes
- Smart router should prefer local nodes by latency (within VPC) else route to dedicated fallback.
- Add routing metadata to requests: x-redwood-customer: zenith-finance; x-redwood-model: rw-fast-1.1-int8; x-redwood-deployment: private-zenith-colo1

CLI snippets (for testing)
# deploy a canary model locally (dev script)
rdwctl deploy --customer zenith-finance --env private --model rw-fast-1.1-int8 --canary 5 --namespace redwood-zenith

# run perf script (short prompts)
./perf/runner.sh --targets 1000 --concurrency 200 --prompts perf/sample_short_prompts.txt --endpoint https://private.redwood.zenith/api/generate

Risks / open questions
- Q: Does Zenith want us to persist KV-cache across restarts? (pros: quicker cold starts; cons: storage of context in customer infra). Need legal input. (Add to ZEN-87).
- Q: Which team owns SSL cert rotation for control plane TLS? They said infra will but need runbook.
- Risk: Hardware constraints in colo — they might not have enough GPU headroom for peak; confirm burst strategy (use Dedicated).

Acceptance criteria for go-live
- End-to-end: deploy + warm model + 48h stable canary (error <1% and p95 latency <150ms).
- Audit logs streaming validated for 7y retention.
- Security signoff (HSM integration & mutual TLS).
- Runbook and escalation path documented and handed to Zenith ops.

Next immediate actions (today)
- Call with Priya to finalize HSM approach (15:00).
- Email SecOps for final CIDR list and control plane egress IPs.
- Draft playbook skeleton for on-prem bootstrap (I will start skeleton under infra/playbooks/zenith-bootstrap.md).

Random reminders for handoff
- Don't check in any real customer secrets into public repos; use placeholders and reference secret manager.
- Add 'zenith' tag to the redwood-monitoring dashboards for easy filtering.

End of scratchpad (will prune later and consolidate into Confluence).
